not_in_the_pack_or_the_handover.what: what this session had to find out for itself in its first ten minutes, starting from start.md, reporter.md, state.json, HANDOVER.md and traces/index.json
items: Who marks the earlier key entry "handed over": the start prompt told the new session to; the old session did it too, a minute earlier (2309e01). Both changed the same lines of data/keys.json and the new session's first release stopped on the conflict. The pack says the entry stays and carries that word, not which session writes it.

The scheduled wake: HANDOVER.md says "set your own"; start.md says the new session's schedule is the conductor's to set. HANDOVER.md does not say at what minute the old session's wake fired, which start.md asks a hand-over to say.

A trace's steps are read by number (incident.journalist@ reads steps[] by n), so an open trace may only grow at the end. Nothing states it as a contract; the role pack lists the journalist as reading only reporter/traces/README.md.

The values of a trace's size (arc, small, medium, large, correction, escalation) are not listed as open or closed anywhere. This session added "outage" after checking that no tool or script in the repository branches on the value.
tools/reporter-fill.mjs needs the tags fetched again at each wake, not once: a commit of the last minutes has no tag in the clone yet and its step's version is written as null without a warning.
reporter/numbers.json can only reach as far as incident.ci@'s last count (03:38 when read at 04:10); neither file says when the next count is due.
The measure step's number is at totals.context_per_call.last in the ledger line; start.md gives it as context_per_call.last.

The role pack cuts board card titles at the first full stop or colon: a-reporter-3 reads "For; waiting on incident.observability@" and j-reporter-1 "Incident.reporter@: each hour", so the card files had to be opened to know what is asked.

A one-line script given to node inside single quotes breaks on an apostrophe ("Dinis Cruz's"); HANDOVER.md warns about backticks in here-documents, the cure is the same: write the script to a file outside the repository.
state.json was not needed (as start.md says for a role that counts the project); the start prompt named it among the files to read. About 2,800 tokens.
